fit_reason: Arista designs and sells high-performance Ethernet switching and routing hardware and software to major internet companies, making it a network chips and switches company in the scale-out layer that links racks across the data center. Networking demand grows as more accelerators are deployed and clusters get larger, and Ethernet is a leading protocol for scale out, so a switch vendor sits directly where the growth is. Cloud and AI data center networking is essentially its whole business, and it is one of the leading suppliers of data center switches to the hyperscalers.

Broadcom supplies Ethernet switch silicon for enterprise and data center networking along with other connectivity chips and optical components, making it a network chips and switches company that also touches optical beyond the rack. Every added accelerator has to be linked in, and Broadcom's switch chips sit inside much of the scale-out and scale-across Ethernet fabric, with exposure to co-packaged optics if CPO scales. Networking is a meaningful part of a business that also includes custom ASICs, wireless chips and infrastructure software, and it is the most important merchant supplier of data center Ethernet switch silicon.

Coherent makes lasers and optical components, and from what is known beyond the description, the current company is a leading maker of datacom transceivers and the lasers inside them, making it an optical-beyond-the-rack company. Optical beyond the rack keeps adding links as clusters grow, and lasers are needed by every optical design whether pluggable or co-packaged, which the guidance singles out as an upside. Optical communications is central to the business alongside industrial lasers and materials, and it is one of the largest suppliers of optical transceivers to AI data centers.

Lumentum makes optical and photonic components for data communications and telecom, including lasers such as VCSELs and modulated lasers, transceivers, transponders and ROADMs, making it an optical-beyond-the-rack company. Optical links beyond the rack keep growing with scale out and scale across, and its lasers are the part needed by every design, positioning it for both pluggables and co-packaged optics. Optical communications is the larger of its two segments and central to the business, and it is a leading supplier of the high-speed lasers used in data center transceivers.

Marvell supplies data center connectivity chips including PAM4 and coherent DSPs, laser drivers, silicon photonics, co-packaged and linear pluggable optics chipsets, active electrical cable DSPs, retimers and Ethernet and UALink scale-up switches, making it both an optical DSP and a network chips company. It spans scale up, scale out and scale across, so it benefits from more optical links beyond the rack, from silicon photonics if CPO scales, and from scale-up switching, although its DSPs are tied to pluggables that co-packaged designs would partly remove. Data center connectivity is central to the business alongside custom ASICs, and it is one of the leading suppliers of optical DSPs to the transceiver industry.

NVIDIA's Compute and Networking segment includes the Mellanox networking and interconnect business, which supplies InfiniBand, Ethernet and the NVLink scale-up links that tie its accelerators together, making it a network chips and switches company at every level of the cluster. Networking keeps accelerators from waiting on each other, and NVLink is the scale-up standard inside the rack while InfiniBand and Ethernet carry scale out, so its networking grows directly with accelerator deployments. Networking is a meaningful part of a business centered on GPUs, and it is one of the most important networking suppliers in AI because it sells the links together with the accelerators.

Credo sells high-speed connectivity for optical and electrical Ethernet, including active electrical cables, optical DSPs and SerDes chiplets and IP, making it both a copper-at-short-reach company and an optical DSP company. Copper remains the existing solution inside the rack and active electrical cables extend its reach as racks get denser, while its DSPs ride the growth of pluggable optics beyond the rack, though co-packaged designs would reduce DSP content. Data center connectivity is essentially its whole business, and it is a leading supplier of active electrical cables to hyperscalers.

Fabrinet provides optical packaging and precision manufacturing for optical communication components, including transceivers, tunable lasers, transponders, ROADMs and active optical cables for data centers and computing clusters, making it an optical-beyond-the-rack company. Its volumes rise as optical links are added for scale out and scale across, and it builds products for whichever optical design customers adopt. Optical communications manufacturing is central to the business, and it is a key contract manufacturer for the leading optical and networking companies.

Astera Labs sells semiconductor connectivity products for cloud and AI infrastructure, covering data, network and memory connectivity, which places it among the network chips companies that tie chips together within and between systems. Faster links between chips and racks let clusters work around memory limits and grow with every accelerator deployed, and scale-up connectivity is a growing part of rack design. AI data center connectivity is its whole business, and it is a fast-growing supplier of retimers and fabric switches to hyperscalers, though smaller than the largest chip vendors.

Ciena supplies coherent optical transport, packet-optical platforms, Waveserver interconnect systems and switching for carrying data across networks, making it an optical-beyond-the-rack company focused on links between data centers. Scale across grows when a single site runs out of power and computing has to be spread across sites and linked, which drives demand for its data center interconnect optics. Optical networking is central to the business, and it is one of the leading suppliers of coherent optical systems, though part of its demand still comes from telecom carriers.

Amphenol makes electrical, electronic and fiber optic connectors, high-speed interconnects, backplane systems and cable assemblies, with information technology and data communication among its markets, making it a copper company that also supplies fiber connectivity. Copper is the existing solution at short reach inside the rack, and every added accelerator needs high-speed connectors and cabling, while optical inside the rack would be gradual. Data communication is a meaningful part of a business that also serves automotive, defense, industrial and mobile markets, and it is one of the largest suppliers of high-speed interconnect for AI racks.

Applied Optoelectronics makes fiber-optic networking products including optical modules, lasers, subassemblies and transceivers, selling to internet data center operators and cable and telecom equipment makers, making it an optical-beyond-the-rack company. Optical links beyond the rack keep growing with cluster size, and it makes its own lasers, which every optical design needs. Optical networking is its whole business, though it is a smaller player than the leading transceiver makers and also depends on cable TV equipment.

Corning provides optical fibers and cables, fiber optic hardware and connectors, cable assemblies and optical components for telecommunications and businesses, making it an optical-beyond-the-rack company at the fiber and connectivity layer. Scale out and scale across both run mostly on optical fiber, so more links between racks and between data centers mean more fiber and connectivity. Optical communications is a meaningful part of a business that also includes display glass, specialty materials, automotive and life sciences, and it is one of the largest optical fiber makers.

Cisco designs IP networking equipment including switching for enterprise campuses and data centers and routing that interconnects networks and data centers, making it a network chips and switches company. Ethernet scale out and scale across grow as clusters get larger, and data center switching and routing put it in that demand, though much of its networking serves enterprise campuses rather than accelerator clusters. Networking is a meaningful part of a business that also includes security, collaboration and observability, and it is one of the largest networking vendors, though less central in AI back-end networks than the leaders.

Celestica provides electronics manufacturing and supplies enterprise data communication infrastructure including routers, switches, data center interconnects and servers to cloud providers including leading hyperscalers, making it a network chips and switches company on the hardware side. Every added accelerator has to be linked in, and the switches it builds for hyperscalers are part of the scale-out fabric. Networking hardware is a meaningful part of a business that also includes servers, storage and other contract manufacturing, and it is a major builder of data center switches for hyperscalers.

Nokia supplies IP routing and a broad optical portfolio including coherent transponders, wavelength-division multiplexers, ROADMs and optical line systems for data center interconnect and long-haul, and counts hyperscalers among its customers, making it an optical-beyond-the-rack and switching company. Scale across grows as computing is spread across sites, which drives demand for its data center interconnect optics and routing. Network infrastructure is a meaningful part of a business that also includes mobile radio networks and licensing, and it is a significant optical and IP networking vendor, though a smaller presence in AI data centers than the leaders.

TE Connectivity makes connectors, cable assemblies, fiber optics and wires and cables, and lists data centers and artificial intelligence among the markets it serves, making it a copper company with some fiber connectivity. Copper remains the existing solution at short reach inside the rack and every added accelerator needs high-speed interconnect, though optical inside the rack could slowly displace part of it. Data center connectivity is a meaningful but minority part of a business led by automotive and industrial markets, and it is a major high-speed interconnect supplier.

Hewlett Packard Enterprise sells networking through its HPE Aruba division, including switches, routers and wired and wireless LAN hardware, and from what is known beyond the description it has added Juniper's data center switching and routing, making it a network chips and switches company. Ethernet scale out grows as clusters get larger, and data center switching and routing give it a share of that demand, although much of its networking serves campus and edge. Networking is a meaningful part of a business centered on servers and storage, and it is a mid-sized networking vendor.

MACOM designs analog semiconductors for wired and wireless connectivity from RF to lightwave, including products for optical networking and data centers, making it an optical-beyond-the-rack component supplier. Optical links beyond the rack keep growing, and the analog drivers and amplifiers inside transceivers scale with them. Data center and optical networking are a meaningful part of a business that also serves telecom, industrial and defense, and it is a notable but second-tier supplier of optical components.

Semtech supplies signal integrity products including optical data communication ICs for data centers, enterprise networks and high-speed interfaces, making it an optical-beyond-the-rack chip supplier. Optical links beyond the rack keep growing, and the signal integrity chips inside transceivers and high-speed links scale with them. Signal integrity is a meaningful part of a business that also includes protection, wireless and IoT products, and it is a smaller supplier than the leading DSP vendors.

AXT makes indium phosphide and gallium arsenide substrates used for data center connectivity lasers, fiber optic lasers and detectors, silicon photonics, photonic integrated circuits and VCSELs, placing it one step upstream of the optical-beyond-the-rack companies. Lasers are needed by every optical design, so more optical links and any shift to silicon photonics both raise demand for the substrates lasers are built on. Substrates for optical devices are a meaningful part of a business that also serves wireless, solar, LEDs and sensing, and it is a small but specialized supplier in the laser supply chain.

Tower Semiconductor is an independent foundry for analog and mixed-signal process technologies including SiGe and RF CMOS, and from what is known beyond the description it is a major foundry for silicon photonics chips used in data center transceivers, making it a supplier to the silicon photonics part of optical beyond the rack. Silicon photonics may gain if co-packaged optics scale, and optical links beyond the rack keep growing, which supports demand for its photonics wafers. Silicon photonics is a meaningful and growing part of a broader foundry business, and its importance in networking rests mostly on its role as a silicon photonics foundry.

Belden supplies copper and fiber cabling, connectivity, interconnect panels, racks and enclosures for local area networks and data centers, plus industrial Ethernet switches, making it a copper and fiber cabling company. More accelerators and larger clusters need more cabling and connectivity, though its products serve general enterprise and data center infrastructure more than accelerator interconnect. Data center connectivity is a meaningful but partial piece of a business spanning enterprise buildings, broadband and industrial automation, and it is a mid-sized cabling supplier.

Extreme Networks designs wired and wireless network infrastructure including aggregation and core switches and data center switches and routers, making it a network chips and switches company. Ethernet scale out grows with cluster size, but most of its business is campus and enterprise networking, so it is only partly exposed to accelerator clusters. Data center switching is a modest part of a networking-focused business, and it is a smaller vendor in data center networking.

MaxLinear makes communications systems-on-chip, including digital signal processing for optical transceivers, alongside broadband, Wi-Fi and wireless infrastructure products, making it a borderline optical DSP company. DSPs are tied to pluggable optics, which keep adding links beyond the rack, though co-packaged designs would largely remove them. Optical transceiver chips are a smaller part of a business centered on broadband and home networking, and it is a minor player in data center optics.

Materion makes engineered materials and, through its Precision Optics segment, thin film coatings, optical filters and integrated assemblies, serving markets that include telecom and data center infrastructure, making it a borderline supplier of optical components. Optical links beyond the rack keep growing, and the filters and coatings used in optical devices grow with them. Optics is a smaller part of a business led by alloys and advanced materials, and its role in networking is as a component supplier rather than a leading player.

Bel Fuse makes power management, circuit protection and interconnect solutions and lists data infrastructure among the industries it serves, making it a borderline copper and connectivity company. Interconnect demand grows as more accelerators and racks are linked, but the description is too thin to say how much of its business is data center networking. Interconnect is one of several product lines, and it is a small supplier in networking.

Dycom provides engineering, construction and installation services for fiber optic, copper and coaxial cable systems for telecommunications providers, and from what is known beyond the description it builds long-haul fiber routes for hyperscalers, making it a borderline fiber company as an installer rather than a maker. Scale across grows when a single site runs out of power and computing has to be spread across sites and linked over fiber, which adds construction work for long-haul routes. Fiber construction is central to the business, but most of it serves telecom and broadband carriers rather than data center links, and it is a large contractor rather than a networking technology supplier.

IES Holdings' Communications segment designs, installs and services network infrastructure, primarily supporting data centers for co-location and managed hosting customers, making it a borderline cabling company as an installer rather than a maker. More data centers and denser racks need more network cabling to be installed, so its communications work grows with data center construction. Network cabling installation is a meaningful part of a business that also includes electrical contracting, infrastructure products and residential work, and it is a regional installer rather than a networking technology supplier.
